meta.source: REFERENCE_2026-10-14_03.49.19.mov (third-party broadcast; screen recording 826x804, 60 fps container)

time_base.unique_frames: only every 5th frame is new (n%5==3): 12 images per video-second; others are exact duplicates
time_base.content_cadence: content advances 2,2,1 units per unique frame (n%15==3 is the short step): 20 units per video-second
time_base.content_T: video-equivalent seconds of content; T(n)=n/60 + {0,1/60,2/60} for n%15 = 3,8,13
time_base.k_status: INFERRED (2,2,1 = 50p->30p decimation, shown at 12 Hz => 0.4x playback; consistent with sprint gait and slide friction); sensitivity k=0.5 given
time_base.real_t_zero: content T=4.65 (frame 278): first non-sole turf contact of the trailing (R) leg

camera_model.note: pinhole fitted to centre circle (r 9.15 m) + halfway line on a stabilised mosaic (ref = frame 288); rms 0.044 m
camera_model.pitch_axes: X along touchline (+ = image right / direction of play), Y along halfway line (+ = away from camera), origin centre spot, metres
camera_model.local_scale_at_tackle: ~69 px/m lateral, ~21 px/m depth, ~66 px/m vertical (1.8 m pole = 122 px); lateral scale +-3%, depth +-6% over fit variants

meta.pitch_coords_caveat: image points are mapped to pitch at an ASSUMED height h (trunk/pelvis) or h~0 for turf contacts; X is insensitive to h (<0.06 m per 1 m), Y is very sensitive (~3 m per 1 m of h error)
meta.LR_convention: slider own perspective; trailing/folded = RIGHT, tackling = LEFT (INFERRED, see report)

summary_metrics.units: m, m/s, m/s^2, s; 'video' = per video-second of content; 'real' assumes k=0.4 (k=0.5 in brackets where useful)

summary_metrics.slide_never_stops: still ~1.4-1.6 m/s video (3.5-4 m/s real) when the get-up begins; on feet by T 8.2-8.3
summary_metrics.front_knee_extension_timing: 95->30 deg flexion over T 4.80-5.00 (0.08 s real); ~6 deg at ball contact f308 (+0.20 s)
summary_metrics.pelvis_descent: monotonic, no hop; shorts-centroid height 0.67 (f263) -> 0.37 (f283) -> 0.30 (f298) -> turf ~f308-313; ~0.3-0.35 s real plant->turf
